name: Cholera & mosquito-borne
summary: WHO counts over 3,000 cholera deaths in 2026, nearly nine in ten in Africa; DR Congo, Sudan and Yemen hard hit
state: WHO said on 10 Nov that more than 3,000 people died of cholera from January to September 2026, nearly nine in ten of them in Africa (SCMP). ECDC's overview of 27 Oct lists DR Congo as the worst-affected country, with Yemen and Afghanistan among those reporting the most new deaths (ECDC), and WHO reported in October that cases were surging in Yemen as conflict intensified (Al Jazeera). Searches on 25 Nov found no sign that these outbreaks in conflict-affected countries are ending, so the Alert holds.
for_you: Risk to UK residents is very low. Travellers to affected areas should follow NHS and NaTHNaC advice on food, water and vaccination, and FCDO travel advice.
rubric_hit: Alert: large high-mortality cholera outbreaks in conflict zones (DR Congo, Sudan, Yemen); over 3,000 deaths in 2026

sources.title: SCMP — Over 3,000 already dead from cholera this year, says WHO
Al Jazeera — Cholera cases surge in Yemen as conflict intensifies, WHO says

why: Climate-sensitive diseases — cholera, dengue, chikungunya, Oropouche, West Nile and yellow fever — are hitting record levels and reaching new regions.
drivers: Conflict, floods, heat, El Niño, water and sanitation, mosquito range expansion.

rubric.alert: Large outbreaks with high mortality in conflict zones, or a WHO grade 3 emergency.
rubric.watch: Record-level seasons, or local transmission in countries where the disease was not established (including Europe).
